BLOCKING — /root/projects/oci-agent-skills/skills/oci-support-limits/scripts/capacity.sh is broken for every non-AD-scoped limit, and it contradicts its own --help. Line 14 makes AD a hard requirement (`: "${AD:?Set AD explicitly; pass it only when scope-type is AD}"`) while line 17 unconditionally appends `--availability-domain "$AD"` to `limits resource-availability get`. Per `oci limits resource-availability get --help`: "This field is mandatory if the scopeType of the target resource limit is AD. Otherwise, this field should be omitted. If the above requirements are not met, the API returns a 400 - InvalidParameter response." Reproduced live 2026-09-09, DEFAULT/us-chicago-1, CLI 3.91.0: `PROFILE=DEFAULT REGION=us-chicago-1 TENANCY_ID=<tenancy> SERVICE=compute LIMIT_NAME=custom-image-count AD=WAGR:US-CHICAGO-1-AD-1 bash skills/oci-support-limits/scripts/capacity.sh` -> calls 1 and 2 return data, call 3 returns `{"kind":"service","status":400}`; the raw CLI gives `InvalidParameter: Parameter 'availabilityDomain' should be null for this limit's scope type.` (status 400). This is exactly the case the skill's own reference warns about — limits-vs-quotas-vs-capacity.md §2 states `custom-image-count` is REGION-scoped and "do not pass one blindly either" — so the script defeats the skill's central teaching, and oci_ro's sanitized envelope hides the reason from the agent. The script's guard message and --help promise conditional behaviour it cannot deliver: line 14's `:?` guard forbids the very omission it tells the caller to make. Fix: make AD optional and append the flag conditionally, e.g. `AD_FLAG=(); [[ -n "${AD:-}" ]] && AD_FLAG=(--availability-domain "$AD")` then pass `"${AD_FLAG[@]}"`, and reword the guard/--help to say AD is required only for AD-scoped limits.
